chunks: My father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa'd ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ammar ibn Abi al-Husayr, said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

There are people among us who believe in the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and consider him superior to all people, but do not describe from your nobility what we have described of your excellence. Should we befriend them? He said to me: Yes, in general. Is it not that God has what the Messenger of God did not have? And the Messenger of God has what we do not have? And we have what you do not have? And you have what others do not have?

Indeed, God the Blessed and Exalted has established Islam upon seven shares: upon patience, truthfulness, certainty, contentment, loyalty, knowledge, and forbearance. Then He divided that among the people. Whoever was given these seven shares is one of perfect faith and endurance. Then He gave some people one share, some two shares, some three shares, some four shares, some five shares, some six shares, and some seven shares.

So do not burden the owner of one share with two shares, nor the owner of two shares with three shares, nor the owner of four shares with five shares, nor the owner of five shares with six shares, nor the owner of six shares with seven shares, lest you burden them and drive them away. But be gentle with them and make the entry easy for them.

And I will give you an example to consider: There was a Muslim man who had a disbelieving neighbor, and the disbeliever was a companion of the believer. The believer desired for the disbeliever to embrace Islam, and he kept beautifying Islam and making it dear to the disbeliever until he accepted Islam. The believer went to him in the morning, took him out of his house, and went with him to the mosque to pray Fajr in congregation with him. When he prayed, he said to him: 'If we sit and remember God, the Exalted, until the sun rises.' So he sat. He said to him: 'If you learned the Quran until the sun passed and fasted today, that would be better.' So he sat with him and fasted until he prayed Dhuhr and Asr. He said: 'If you endured until you prayed Maghrib and the late Isha, that would be better.' So he sat with him until he prayed Maghrib and the late Isha. Then they rose, and his effort had reached its limit and he was burdened with what he could not bear.

So when it was the next day, he went to him intending to do to him what he had done the previous day, and knocked on his door, then said to him: 'Come out so we can go to the mosque.' He answered him: 'Turn away from me, for this is a strict religion that I cannot bear.'

So do not strain them. Do you not know that the rule of the Banu Umayya was with the sword, force, and oppression? And indeed, our rule is with gentleness, affinity, dignity, concealment, good companionship, piety, and striving. So attract the people to your religion and to what you are in.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّة: Concealment or prudence in religious practice

ai.seo_question: How should Muslims interact with those who have different levels of religious commitment and capacity?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the concept of *al-As'hāb* (the shares), explaining that spiritual perfection is graded rather than uniform, with the seven pillars of Islam distributed among believers according to their capacity. This theological framework justifies the Imams' political strategy of *al-Taqiyya* and gentleness, contrasting it with the Umayyads' use of force, to prevent overwhelming the masses and driving them away from the faith. The narrative underscores the practical wisdom of gradual spiritual elevation, ensuring that religious obligations remain accessible and manageable for the general community.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 7-36 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Mahboob, on the authority of Am’mar ibn Abil Ahvas, “Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) was asked, ‘There are people amongst us who believe in the Caliphate of the Commander of the Faithful (MGB), and consider him to be superior to all people, but do not believe in your nobility as we do. Should we be friends with them?’ Imam as-Sadiq (MGB) replied, ‘Yes, absolutely. Is it not true that God has things that the Prophet of God doesn’t have? Is it not true that the Prophet of God has things that we do not have? Is it not true thatwe have things that you do not have? Is it not true that you have things that others do not have?

God the Blessed the Sublime has partitioned Islam into seven parts, and has distributed them amongst the people. These are perseverance, honesty, certitude, contentment, loyalty, knowledge, and patience. Whoever possesses all seven has perfect faith and is strong. He gave some people just one, some just two, some just three, some just four, some just five, some just six, and some all seven of these. Therefore, you should not expect one who has only been given one part of the faith to be responsible for two parts.

You cannot burden one who has been granted only two parts of the faith with what you would ask from those who have three parts of faith. And so on. If you expect too much of them, they will be over-burdened and might turn away from the religion. Instead you should be patient and treat them with kindness, and make things easy for them.

Now I will cite an example for you. There was a Muslim man with an infidel neighbor who was his friend. The man wished to help his friend become a Muslim. He kept trying to show him how nice Islam was, and insisted on his becoming a Muslim. Finally, he managed, and the man accepted Islam. The next morning the man went to his neighbor’s house, and asked him to accompany him to the morning congregation prayer. They went there and when the prayer ended he told the new Muslim man to sit down and recite the Quran until sunrise. They stayed there, and continued reciting until sunrise. Then he told him it was nice to fast that day and study the Quran until noon. The new Muslim agreed. After the noon and afternoon prayers, he suggested to the new Muslim man to stay there until dawn, to say their prayers in the mosque and then go home at night. He agreed.

They did their night prayer, got up and went home. The next morning the man went to his neighbor’s house again and asked him to go to the mosque. The man said, ‘Leave me alone. This religion is too difficult. I cannot stand it.’

Therefore you should learn not to pressure the people. Do you know that the rule of the Umayyad clan was based upon force, the sword and oppression? However, we rule the people’s hearts with patience, kindness, concealing of faith, good association, piety, and struggling. Try to attract the people to your religion.’”
